name: econdash
description: 750+ indicators in ten categories: macroeconomics, financial markets, labor, demographics, real estate, commodities and energy, transport and logistics, healthcare, education, technology and internet. 290+ countries and regions, from the World Bank, IMF, FRED, Eurostat, OECD, WHO and other public sources. Every figure comes with its source, licence and a link to the EconDash chart.

interface.longDescription:
EconDash brings a catalogue of public statistics into the conversation: 750+ indicators for 290+ countries and regions in ten categories: macroeconomics, financial markets, labor, demographics, real estate, commodities and energy, transport and logistics, healthcare, education, technology and internet. The data comes from the World Bank, IMF, FRED, Eurostat, ECB, OECD, WHO, BIS and other public sources.

What you can ask
- The latest value or the history of an indicator for a country: GDP growth in Germany, CPI inflation in Japan, youth unemployment in South Africa.
- A comparison of up to 20 countries on one indicator, for a given year or the latest observation.
- Which indicators exist on a topic, such as house prices, energy or internet use.
- The source, licence, unit, frequency and coverage of an indicator, to cite it correctly.

Every value comes with its period, unit, source and licence, and a link to the EconDash chart page with the full series. When a country, year or indicator has no data, EconDash says so and names the periods or countries that have data; it does not fill the gap. Forecasts, such as IMF projections, are labelled.

Who it is for
Analysts, journalists, students, teachers and researchers who need sourced figures in a conversation, and developers who need the same data while they work in Codex.

Limitations
- Read-only: EconDash does not change anything in your accounts or on the web.
- One answer holds up to 30 annual values or about ten years of monthly or quarterly data; the linked chart page shows the whole series. Signing in to an EconDash account with full data access returns longer histories in one answer.
- Series follow the release schedule of their source; most are annual, quarterly or monthly. EconDash is not a live market feed: it has no intraday quotes and no series for individual shares or cryptocurrencies, and it does not publish forecasts or news of its own.
- Indicator names and data are in English; questions can be in any language.
capabilities: Latest values and history by country
Compare up to 20 countries on one indicator
Source, licence and coverage of every series
defaultPrompt: Use EconDash to get Germany's GDP growth for the last ten years.
What does EconDash say about Japan's CPI inflation?
Pull Brazil's total fertility rate from EconDash for 2000 to 2024.

positive.description: Latest decade of one indicator for one country. The answer is a table of annual values with the unit, the source (World Bank) and a link to the EconDash chart.
positive.prompt: Use EconDash to get Germany's GDP growth for the last ten years.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the indicator gdp-growth-annual-percent, gets the ten latest annual values for DEU and shows them with the unit, source and chart link.

positive.description: Comparison of three countries on one indicator, latest observation in each.
positive.prompt: Use EconDash to compare the sex ratio at birth in Turkey, Ukraine and Israel.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds sex-ratio-m-f and compares TUR, UKR and ISR: one value per country with its year, the source and a chart link for each.

positive.description: Metadata for citing a series: source, publisher, licence and coverage.
positive.prompt: What is the source and licence of EconDash's life expectancy data?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds life-expectancy-at-birth and states its source and publisher, licence, attribution text, unit, frequency and years covered.

positive.prompt: Search EconDash for indicators on house prices.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists house price indicators (for example the house price index and residential property prices) with unit, frequency, source and years covered.

positive.description: Full history for a signed-in user. Uses the reviewer account; without sign-in the plugin asks the user to sign in and offers the latest values instead.
positive.prompt: Give me US GDP per capita for every year since 1960.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds gdp-per-capita and returns every annual value for USA from 1960 to the latest year, with the unit, source and chart link.

negative.description: Live price of a single share. EconDash has no series for individual shares, so it should not be called; the model answers with another tool or says it has no live quote.
negative.prompt: What is Apple's stock price today?

negative.description: A definition that needs no data. The model answers from its own knowledge without calling EconDash.
A creative task with no statistics. EconDash is not called.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about money.

publication.release_notes: First release for ChatGPT and Codex: six read-only tools for searching the catalogue, getting a country's values, comparing countries and citing sources, and three skills: macro-research, compare-economies and cite-economic-data.
